label: rem:vol-as-motivic-period
title: $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ as a motivic period: the Bloch--Wigner regulator reading of $\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}$
html:
Period interpretation. The hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) is a motivic period: the value of a mixed-Tate motive under the Bloch-Wigner regulator r_\infty. For a hyperbolic knot complement with shape parameters z_i, the volume is:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{k} D(z_i),

where D is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. Each D(z_i) is a Kontsevich-Zagier period. For motivic periods and the action of the motivic Galois group on them, in the basic case of the motivic fundamental group of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, 1, \infty\}, whose periods are the multiple zeta values, see [brown-motivic-p1-three-points, §1].

Regulator interpretation. The shape parameters define a class [K] \in \mathcal{B}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) in the pre-Bloch group, yielding:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  r_\infty\bigl([K]\bigr).

The volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the K-theoretic image of an algebraic class under a transcendental regulator.

QOU placement. The archimedean realization functor factorizes across three pictures: adelic projection (\pi_\infty \circ \tau), Euler-characteristic integration (\pi_\infty \circ \chi_{\mathrm{top}}), and Bloch-Wigner regulation (r_\infty). These pictures agree on the algebraic quantum volume domain. Each formalizes a distinct aspect: adelic ensures categorical compatibility, Euler-characteristic handles blow-up calculus, and Bloch-Wigner bridges to quantum topology literature.
